title: Choose a visual direction for the Showoff prelaunch page
question: Which direction should shape the marketing page? What should carry forward, what feels false to Showoff, and should the selected concept be approved, combined, revised, or rejected?

options.label: Job Ticket Route
options.lineage: Numbered work tickets on a neighborhood print-shop rail
options.thesis: One ticket links every step of a small business’s marketing run.
options.viewport: A wide work ticket introduces Showoff, names the seven marketing stages, and ends in one clear waitlist action.
options.risk: The print artifact can feel nostalgic if the workflow is only decoration.

raised.raise: State remains legible through labels and shape, never color alone.

options.label: Teletext Service Index
options.thesis: A numbered service index lays the marketing workflow out in scan-ready rows.
options.viewport: A service index introduces Showoff and lays the seven marketing stages out as numbered destinations.
options.case: Product clarity holds: numbered rows make the workflow scannable; the broadcast form is less recognizable to small-business owners.
options.risk: It reads as retro novelty when the grid is not strict.

options.label: Punch-Card Weave
options.thesis: A marketing workflow woven from instructions into a visible finished pattern.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the textile subject is not familiar to the broad small-business audience, and the woven metaphor obscures Showoff’s product.
options.risk: A craft metaphor can hide the direct marketing job.
options.kept: Every stage should remain traceable through the workflow.

options.label: Hand-Processed Film Strip
options.thesis: A creative process shown frame by frame through its making.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the audience may recognize creative tools, but the film form competes with explaining the complete Showoff workflow.
options.risk: Wear and light leaks can dominate product clarity.
options.kept: The page can reveal the product sequence in deliberate stages.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Marketing stages appear as a shared board of time-sensitive departures.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the board suggests changing announcements, not a customer's full marketing work.
options.risk: The letter-flip effect can become the entire story.
options.kept: State labels should be plain and immediately scannable.

options.label: Reverse-Perspective Cabinet
options.thesis: A set of marketing tools opens outward like a painted cabinet.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an inventory of objects does not explain how Showoff connects the marketing workflow.
options.risk: The cabinet may read as decorative product illustration.
options.kept: Keep the full set of workflow capabilities visible together.

options.label: Panel-Wrapped Racing Vinyl
options.thesis: A single oversized creative idea carries across connected marketing panels.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the loud vehicle form is remote from the everyday job of planning and running small-business marketing.
options.risk: The spectacle can overpower the product explanation.
options.kept: Connected stages should feel like parts of one system.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clear marketing page explains the product and makes the waitlist easy to join.
canonCard.viewport: A direct headline, a short product explanation, the seven-stage workflow, and one waitlist form.
canonCard.risk: It may feel familiar by design.
